_note: Every fact in atp.json points at keys here. 'checked' says what was read and when. The machine's counts (8 c-subunits, 8 protons and 3 ATP per turn) come only from watt-2010. 'calc' numbers were measured by tools/hero_atp_build.py from the local 1MAB file. Shapes and sizes of the membrane, ring, stalks and a-subunit are drawn, not measured.

os-7-4.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: complex I pumps hydrogen ions from the matrix into the intermembrane space, building a gradient across the inner membrane; hydrogen ions can only pass back through the inner membrane by an integral membrane protein called ATP synthase, which acts as a tiny generator turned by the hydrogen ions diffusing through it down their electrochemical gradient; chemiosmosis makes 90 percent of the ATP made during aerobic glucose catabolism.

motm-72.cite: Goodsell, D. (2005). Molecule of the Month: ATP Synthase. RCSB PDB-101, December 2005.
motm-72.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: ATP synthase is two motors in one machine; F0 is an electric motor embedded in the membrane, F1 a chemical motor; protons flowing through F0 turn a circular rotor; in the bacterial F0 shown, the rotor has 12 identical chains and the ion pump is a single chain.

watt-2010.cite: Watt, I. N., Montgomery, M. G., Runswick, M. J., Leslie, A. G. and Walker, J. E. (2010). Bioenergetic cost of making an adenosine triphosphate molecule in animal mitochondria. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 107, 16823-16827.
watt-2010.checked: 2026-10-01, abstract read (Europe PMC, PMID 20847295): the catalytic domain sticks out into the mitochondrial matrix and is joined to the membrane domain by central and peripheral stalks; the central stalk and a ring of c-subunits turn about 100 times per second; each c-subunit carries a glutamate near the middle of the membrane on the ring's outer surface, and the turning comes from protonating and deprotonating each glutamate in turn; each full turn makes three ATP and moves one proton per c-subunit; in cow (bovine) mitochondria the ring has eight c-subunits; vertebrate c-subunits are nearly identical, so vertebrates probably have 8-rings too, needing 2.7 protons per ATP; fungi, eubacteria and chloroplasts have rings of 10 to 15.

rcsb-1MAB.checked: 2026-10-01, local mmCIF file read by tools/hero_atp_build.py: one alpha (501 of 510 residues modelled), one beta (477 of 479) and the gamma chain (124 of 270 residues modelled), plus ATP, ADP, one magnesium and one phosphate; assembly 1 applies the crystal three-fold turns (operators 1 and 2) to alpha, beta and the ligands, giving three alpha and three beta around one gamma. Also see ../molecules/sources.json (X-ray, 2.8 angstrom, Rattus norvegicus).

bianchet-1998.cite: Bianchet, M. A., Hullihen, J., Pedersen, P. L. and Amzel, L. M. (1998). The 2.8-A structure of rat liver F1-ATPase: configuration of a critical intermediate in ATP synthesis/hydrolysis. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 95, 11065-11070.
bianchet-1998.checked: 2026-10-01, entry in ../molecules/sources.json: citation read from the 1MAB mmCIF file.

calc.cite: Measured by this app's tools/hero_atp_build.py from the local 1MAB mmCIF file.
calc.checked: 2026-10-01: the full head built from assembly 1 has 22,655 atoms (no water); the ring of three alpha and three beta chains is 12.1 nm across its three-fold axis and 10.6 nm tall along it; the modelled part of gamma is 10.3 nm long and sticks out 1.9 nm beyond the ring on one side.
